Needs a direct check against the current portland.gov Heritage Tree database or a street-level photo before shipping or blocking. Same ambiguity as objectid 100: described as 'east tree in a row of three Elms' at an address where two other register rows (85, 170) explicitly record a 2013 removal of a grove of 3. Needs direct current-status confirmation before shipping or blocking.

Paired Heritage Pine at the same address as objectid 193, which the register explicitly marks dead/removed 2016. This row (311) carries no removal note itself, but was not independently checked this pass; confirm before shipping. [2026-09-27 verify pass: searched Laurelhurst Neighborhood Association coverage specifically; found general Heritage Tree program mentions but nothing confirming this specific tree, alive, independent of the register. Still needs ground-truth given the paired dead tree at the same address.]

Not selected for this pass: isolated in Hillsdale, 4.1km from centre, well outside the walkable cluster this pass focused on. Register describes it as 'over 160 years old... great historical significance, being an Oregon State Heritage Tree and recognized by the Home Orchard Society', possibly the last tree of an 1847 orchard planted by Gideon Tibbetts. Strong candidate for a future depth pass on Portland; not evidence-rejected, just not chosen for the initial 10.

One of three Heritage London Planetrees (396, 314, 321) in a small pocket park; a genuine compact ensemble like the Eliot Hawthorns, but 3.5km north of the downtown cluster this pass prioritised. Good candidate for a future 'Overlook' mini-walk together with the Northern Red Oak at nearby Patton Square (por-list did not include either).

CONFIRMED ALIVE AND CURRENT: this exact tree (Patton Square Park, 5340 N Interstate Ave) is one of the 12 trees NEWLY designated as a City Heritage Tree in the City of Portland's 2026 ordinance (https://www.portland.gov/council/documents/ordinance/2026-heritage-trees), so its live status is unusually well confirmed. Not selected for the 10 only because it sits 4.6km from the downtown cluster, isolated from the other Overlook candidates' immediate area by about 1km. Strong candidate for a future Overlook-area walk. [2026-09-27 verify pass: found a CycleBlaze travel blog that names this tree only as a historical cross-reference to an earlier undetailed outing, not a first-hand observation. Not enough. Still needs a genuine second source.]

leads.name: Powell Butte Cedar Grove Douglas-fir
leads.address: Cedar Grove Trail, Powell Butte Nature Park
leads.access: Free. Public nature park (Portland Water Bureau land, managed with Parks as Powell Butte Nature Park); tree is along the Cedar Grove Trail.
leads.reason: [2026-10-03 write pass] Verified (register treeid 260, alive per iNaturalist 2026-03-22) but held back from publication: the register coordinate has only 4 decimals, so the pin is approximate, and there is no photograph, so preflight's photo-or-pin check refuses it. Publish once a photograph or a confirmed pin on the Cedar Grove Trail exists. Verify notes: Register only (designated 2004): 166 ft tall (about 50 m), 56 ft spread, 71 in diameter, 18.8 ft circumference. Register note: 'located along the Cedar Grove Trail in Powell Butte Nature Park.' Register coordinate has only 4 decimals (about 10 m), so approximate; the trail location is the honest direction. Alive: lifecheck RECENT, iNaturalist obs 2026-03-22 (https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/344523182) near the coordinate. Second Powell Butte tree already published (ptl_012, Lombardy poplar). Tallest and thickest unmined Douglas-fir in the register. No age in source.
